checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_receipt's type-dispatch logic explicitly handle all transaction types without silent fall-through to legacy encoding?

reachability.notes: Silent fall-through for future transaction types would produce incorrect receipt encodings.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the encode_receipt function and locate its isinstance type-dispatch chain. 2. Enumerate all transaction types currently supported in the codebase (LegacyTransaction, AccessListTransaction, DynamicFeeTransaction, BlobTransaction, etc.). 3. Verify each transaction type has an explicit branch in the isinstance chain. 4. Check if the final else/fall-through branch raises an exception or has defensive assertions. 5. Create a mock transaction type that does not match any isinstance check and verify encode_receipt raises an explicit error rather than silently encoding as legacy. 6. Review the order of isinstance checks to ensure no type can be incorrectly matched by a parent class check. 7. Search for any new transaction types added in recent commits that may not yet be in the dispatch chain.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0039, Trust Boundary: tb-029. This is an invariant property: the isinstance fall-through path MUST only be reached for genuine LegacyTransaction instances. Silent misencoding of receipts for unrecognized transaction types causes consensus failures that are extremely difficult to debug. PoC approach: introduce a mock transaction type not in the isinstance chain and show encode_receipt produces legacy encoding instead of raising an error.

checklist.title: Verify P2P/Transaction Boundary: Are receipts from external peers validated against expected transaction types before processing?

reachability.notes: Silent fall-through for future transaction types would produce incorrect receipt encodings.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace data flow from P2P receipt reception to encode_receipt invocation. 2. Identify all validation checkpoints between external input and encoding logic. 3. Verify that transaction type validation occurs before encode_receipt is called. 4. Test boundary by sending crafted P2P messages with unusual transaction type indicators. 5. Verify the execution client properly rejects or handles unknown transaction types at the boundary before they reach encode_receipt.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0039, Supporting check for boundary edge tb-029 covering actor-execution-client and actor-p2p-peer. External peers could potentially introduce transactions with unrecognized types that bypass validation.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is block header timestamp strictly validated to be greater than parent timestamp?

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer could manipulate the timestamp field within the block header.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all code paths where block headers are received via P2P network. 2. Locate the timestamp validation logic in header verification. 3. Verify the comparison is strictly greater-than (not greater-than-or-equal). 4. Attempt to submit a block with timestamp equal to parent timestamp and verify rejection. 5. Attempt to submit a block with timestamp less than parent timestamp and verify rejection. 6. Check for integer overflow edge cases in timestamp comparison. 7. Verify that the parent block reference cannot be spoofed to bypass validation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0040, Trust Boundary: tb-023. Pre-condition: forall (header, parent): header.timestamp > parent.timestamp. Timestamp manipulation enables MEV extraction and disrupts block ordering invariants. PoC target: demonstrate a block with timestamp <= parent.timestamp that passes header validation.

checklist.title: Verify header_construction subgraph correctly enforces timestamp ordering invariant

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer could manipulate the timestamp field within the block header.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the data flow from actor-execution-client through actor-block-builder to actor-parent-block. 2. Verify that timestamp validation occurs before any block processing logic. 3. Check that the parent block's timestamp is retrieved from a trusted source (not from the incoming block header). 4. Verify that validation failure results in immediate rejection without side effects. 5. Ensure error messages do not leak information useful for timing attacks.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0040, Supporting check for SG-004 (header_construction). Covered nodes: actor-execution-client, actor-block-builder, actor-parent-block.
